doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Special Edition personnel changes
summary: Peter Warren is replaced by Rufus Reid and horns come and go, with drum machines and synthesizers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Then this group, “Special Edition” goes through various evolutions as well because when David and Black Arthur Blythe leave then Chico Freeman and John Purcell come in. So, continually evolving but maintaining your vision for an ensemble sound, continuing to write for these groups. Do you want to talk about that evolution and what that leads to at this point?
Yeah… The change of personnel. Peter Warren leaves, and he was replaced by Rufus Reid. For a while we had Chico, Purcell and Murray I believe.
So you had a three (horn) frontline then?
Yeah… Then I added Howard Johnson.

When Rufus joined it was Howard, Rufus, John Purcell and David Murray. I wrote for that group using some electric drum machines and synthesizers. I did something called, “The New Orleans Strut,” which was really nice and I recorded it again on an album with… It was “Pretty Boy” Purdie’s record. He and I both played drums on
